clue.text: Demanding rent is infuriating!

indicators.note: rent here is the past participle of rend, torn apart, so the word before it is ripped up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A tenant fumes at a landlord who asks for exorbitant rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like the money a landlord demands, but it means torn: DEMANDING torn apart becomes MADDENING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something maddening drives a person mad with annoyance, which is exactly what infuriating means.

clue.text: Alert the USA maybe by importing ore intermittently

indicators.note: importing means bringing in from outside, so letters are put inside the other piece
intermittently means at intervals, so the imported letters go in at separate points rather than as one block
maybe signals one possible form of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; intermittently says its letters go in at intervals

explanation.surface: Warn America by bringing in ore now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: USA is rearranged to AUS, and the letters of ORE are dropped in at intervals: A, RO, US, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone is to rouse them to attention, so arouse is a fair verb synonym.

clue.text: Honour rank

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an academic award, such as an honours qualification from a university
second meaning: a level or step in a scale of status

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a university qualification conferred as an honour and a grade or level of standing.

clue.text: Ten in unknown novel of great age

indicators.note: novel means new, so the preceding words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tenth part of an obscure book about extreme old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten in' looks like a container instruction, but both words are anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching ninety years is regarded as a very old age for a person.

clue.text: City falls

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Falls, a city on the US-Canada border
second meaning: the famous waterfalls on the ... River

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the great waterfalls and to the border cities named after them.

clue.text: Empty head with thunder rolling in one of a large number of equal parts

definitions.text: one of a large number of equal parts

indicators.note: rolling things tumble over, so these letters are tossed into a new order
emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A storm makes someone's head go blank as it rumbles overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth is one of a hundred equal parts, and a hundred counts as a large number.

clue.text: Face left, turn and run! That's working well

indicators.note: colours that run spread and lose their shape, so all these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Drill commands: face left, about turn, and run; that seems to get results.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like parade-ground orders; FACE and LEFT stay whole, and a turn supplies U from U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Effectual means producing the intended effect, so something effectual is working well.

clue.text: Anticipate worker, excited about what's coming

parts.note: the worker ant, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An employee looks forward eagerly to what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectant describes someone eagerly awaiting an event, keyed up about what is to come.

clue.text: Get the best of wily creature getting away first

parts.note: out means away, escaped; first places it at the front

explanation.surface: A hunted fox escapes and beats its pursuers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the word for getting away goes in front of the creature, even though the creature comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To outfox someone is to outwit or beat them by cunning, so it means to get the better of them.

clue.text: Agreeable company's unfortunate leaning

parts.note: Co is the standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: an unfortunate thing has gone wrong, so the word after it is in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A firm has an unhappy bias that might not please anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial company is pleasant and suited to one's taste, so the word is a synonym of agreeable.

clue.text: Stick to edited header

indicators.note: an edited text has been reworked, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor is told not to change a page heading that has been revised.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay attached, the same as to stick.

clue.text: Entail alteration to stern of oriental ship — that's vital

indicators.note: an alteration changes something, so the letters of entail are reordered

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Changing the back end of an Eastern vessel is said to be crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To stern of' says the rearranged ENTAIL goes behind E and SS: ESS then ENTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable or absolutely necessary, the same as vital.

clue.text: Keep previously cancelled hold on former musical group

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let a deleted word stand
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: An editor reinstates a struck-out booking of a band from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: STET, Latin for 'let it stand', is written beside a crossed-out word to keep it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six musicians, so it is one kind of musical group.

clue.text: Understand and put under arrest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grasp or perceive
second meaning: to seize and take into custody

explanation.surface: A police officer grasps the situation and makes an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to grasp mentally and, in law enforcement, to seize a suspect.

clue.text: New energy, one third depleted, gets a top up

indicators.note: depleted means used up, and one third of the word's six letters are lost from it

parts.note: taken as written; its last two of six letters go

explanation.surface: Someone running low on energy gets a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: A freshener is British slang for a top-up drink, which freshens a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshener is something that refreshes, such as a fresh round poured into a glass, a top-up.

clue.text: Questionable change to a bed on board

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the following letters into another order

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Whether to swap a bed for a board is in doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Debatable means open to argument or dispute, so it is questionable.

clue.text: Bounder involved in decadence

indicators.note: something involved in a word is caught up inside it, so the answer lies within the next word

parts.note: letters three to five of this word

explanation.surface: A rotter takes part in a life of decadence.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounder and cad are both old-fashioned British words for a dishonourable man.

clue.text: About university's second-class youngster?

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A query about a second-rate student at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a cub is a youngster only in a loose sense: a young animal, or a novice reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cub is the young of a fox, bear or lion, and by extension a young or junior person.

clue.text: A farm is lost when farmyard lacks irrigation

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the adjective describing it

indicators.note: weak signal: the leftover letters must be rearranged with no clearer instruction
something lost is gone, so these letters are taken away from the longer word

explanation.surface: A drought strikes and a farm fails because its yard has no water.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and FARM from FARMYARD leaves Y, R, D, which then have to be reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that receives no irrigation or rain is dry, without moisture.

clue.text: Hit back at goddess, no small upstart

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction, so the word for hit is read right to left
no means without, so the abbreviation for small is taken out of the goddess

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone strikes back at a goddess, who is no little upstart herself.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a person who has risen suddenly in wealth or status without acceptance, an upstart.

clue.text: Retain right new way to learn a different skill

indicators.note: putting things in a new way means arranging them differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Advice to keep the right fresh approach when picking up new skills.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to be trained again, acquiring a new skill or trade.

clue.text: Tree in alcove

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the laurel tree whose leaves flavour cooking
second meaning: a recess in a wall or room

explanation.surface: A tree is growing in a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the laurel tree and a recessed section such as a bay window.

clue.text: Mariner's sole seafood?

explanation.surface: A sailor's flatfish is his only catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' wants to be the fish; it means only. The question mark notes that seafood is a category the answer belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, eaten as seafood especially in Asia and California.

clue.text: Rogue artist's state

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist; the plural or possessive gives an extra S
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A painter's condition is described as that of a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, the same as a rogue.

clue.text: Whale with a bulge, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints at one possible arrangement, so these letters may be reordered

explanation.surface: A whale with a protruding lump, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: The beluga really has a bulging forehead, the melon, so the surface describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a small white Arctic whale.

clue.text: Bad French ruler in Spanish town

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander or ruler

explanation.surface: A wicked French king lives in a Spanish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a port city on Spain's Costa del Sol in Andalusia.

clue.text: Warning call outside old city creates a rumpus

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of a ball in flight
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A shout of warning beyond an ancient city's walls causes an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outbreak of public anger or excitement, a commotion or rumpus.

clue.text: Aspect to assess for apparent worth

parts.note: a face is one side or aspect, as of a problem
to value is to estimate the worth of

explanation.surface: An appraiser looks at one facet when judging how much something seems worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Face value is the worth printed on a coin or the apparent merit of something taken at first sight.

clue.text: Asinine sound man uttered initially had a whine

indicators.note: something uttered is said out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: he is a man; spoken, it is the sound spelt as a drawn-out syllable

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: first letters of had, a and whine

explanation.surface: A man spoke first and had a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Asinine here is literal: it means of an ass, so the sound is a donkey's bray.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haw imitates the bray of a donkey, the sound an ass makes.

clue.text: Perhaps adult in another room is a pitch adjuster

indicators.note: in puts one set of letters inside the other
perhaps suggests one possible version of the word, so its letters may be rearranged

parts.note: the outer fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: another version of a word is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the inner fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Maybe a grown-up in the next room is the one turning the music up or down.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word is rearranged on its own before one goes inside the other, so treating the whole phrase as a single anagram hides the structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A modulator is a device or circuit that varies a signal, such as altering its pitch.

clue.text: Goad the French want first

parts.note: to want is to need; first puts it at the front

explanation.surface: An instruction to provoke the French, who want to go first.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or irritate them persistently, which is what goading is.

clue.text: Split seed apart, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the words are just one possible arrangement, so their letters can be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gardener splits a seed open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' and 'apart' both look like part of the meaning, but apart is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is the past participle meaning divided, and separated means divided into parts.
